key_concepts: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of one or more solutes dissolved in a solvent.
The solute is the substance that is dissolved in a solution.
The solvent is the substance that dissolves the solute.
Solutions can exist in solid, liquid, or gas phases depending on the state of the solvent.
Air is a gaseous solution whose solvent is nitrogen gas.
Steel is a solid solution with iron as the solvent and carbon as the solute.
Vinegar is a solution formed from acetic acid and water.
Solution particles are not visible to the naked eye.
Solutions do not scatter a beam of light.
The solute in a solution cannot be separated by filtration or mechanical means.
Any two substances that mix evenly to form a single phase may form a solution.
Common household examples of solutions include soda, vinegar, and wine.
